Project goals and
how the application achieved them

Problem Room is a completed local teacher/student practice application. This deck covers ten goals supported by the current repository, rather than a future roadmap. Source: README.md; ARCHITECTURE.md; backend/main.py. The cover artwork is a conceptual illustration generated for this presentation. It is not a product screenshot or a record of an actual classroom. The presentation uses the app’s cream, forest-green, and gold visual palette.

Individual practice,
managed by a teacher

Maintain the shared bank.
Choose each student’s problem list.
Update assignments when needed.

Open assigned problems.
Browse the shared bank.
Check answers and explanations.
One shared bank supports a different practice list for every student.

The main accomplished goal is a teacher-managed practice platform. Students and teachers use one first-name/grade login form. The returned stored role selects the frontend view, and backend dependencies separately enforce permissions. Teachers select a student and save a complete question-ID selection. Students can also explore the shared bank independently. Sources: frontend/index.html; frontend/app.js openRoom, loadTeacher, loadStudent; backend/routers/assignments.py; backend/services/assignments.py. The application stores current assignments and gives immediate feedback. It does not claim measured improvements in learning outcomes.

A distinct problem set
for each student

A JavaScript Set retains IDs
from every bank page.

01   Choose a student

02   Select bank questions

03   Save the complete selection
PUT /api/assignments/{student_id} replaces the student’s saved list.

How achieved: frontend/app.js state.selected is a Set independent of state.questions, which contains only the visible page. loadSelection fetches current assignments and fills that Set. Save sends every selected ID in one PUT /api/assignments/{student_id} request. AssignmentUpdate validates at most 100 strict positive IDs; an empty list clears the current set. services/assignments.py replace validates the student and every question ID before deleting old links, adds the desired deduplicated set, then commits once. Invalid selections preserve the old list. The additive POST endpoint separately supports the Cartesian product of selected students and questions. Evidence: tests/test_assignments.py; tests/frontend-pagination.test.cjs first test.
A problem from the included bank

How many positive integers
are divisors of 6000?
Students can check repeatedly. Feedback stays on the current page.

How achieved: frontend studentCard builds the appropriate answer input, converts true/false selection into an actual boolean, and posts response to /api/bank/questions/{question_id}/check. CheckAnswer validates the general shape. services/questions.py check_answer loads the row, validates response type and MCQ membership, then calls the pure grading dispatch function. AnswerFeedback returns is_correct, correct_answer, and explanation. No answer/attempt table or database commit occurs. Students may check any bank question, including unassigned ones. Example source: data/competition_problems.json entry for NZMOC Sample Number Theory #1 by Ross Atkins. The 6000 divisor explanation comes from that included data. Evidence: tests/test_bank.py repeatability and no-write assertions; tests/test_grading.py.

One reusable bank,
three question formats
Teacher CRUD updates the shared bank. Assigned lists use the same question rows.

How achieved: backend/routers/questions.py provides teacher-only POST/GET/PUT/DELETE operations. schemas.py QuestionCreate is a discriminated union selected by the type field. MCQCreate requires 2–6 choices, unique IDs, and a key matching a choice ID. TrueFalseCreate requires StrictBool. ShortAnswerCreate requires a nonempty list of accepted strings. services/questions.py creates, fully replaces, or deletes the original Question ORM row. services/grading.py compares exact MCQ IDs, exact booleans, or normalized short-answer aliases. The pure MCQ grader does no trimming, while request validation may trim incoming strings first. Short-answer comparison does not infer mathematical equivalence. Sources: backend/schemas.py; backend/services/questions.py; backend/services/grading.py. Evidence: tests/test_questions.py; tests/test_grading.py.

Search and pagination
keep the bank usable

Search prompt text or topic.

Apply an exact topic filter.

Count matches before paging.

Render only the visible page.
Pagination test fixture: 45 results appear as pages of 20, 20, and 5.

How achieved: QuestionFilters validates q/topic/type and page/page_size. services/questions.py list_questions builds SQL filters first, counts the filtered subquery, computes the last page, clamps an oversized requested page, then applies ORDER BY id with LIMIT/OFFSET. Substring search escapes % and _ so they act as literal user characters. Both bank routes return arrays plus X-Total-Count and X-Page headers. The frontend reads these headers and renders the visible cards. Its topic dropdown queries a distinct whole-bank topic list. The API also supports question-type filtering, although the student UI exposes text and topic controls. The 45-row example is an isolated test fixture, not the live bank count or a performance benchmark. Sources: backend/services/questions.py; frontend/app.js request/loadStudent/loadTeacherPage. Evidence: tests/test_pagination.py; tests/frontend-pagination.test.cjs.

Validated imports
expand the problem library

Validate the whole file first.
Skip exact prompt duplicates.
Preserve existing assignments.

Discover bulk Parquet files.
Select usable integer-answer problems.
Deduplicate by source ID.
Both paths reuse the question schemas and commit the collected batch once.

How achieved: backend/import_problems.py uses TypeAdapter(list[QuestionCreate]).validate_json to validate every local entry before adding rows, deduplicates exact prompt text, and commits once. It includes a default set of 12 NZMOC problems with credit and license information. backend/import_online.py discovers MathNet Parquet files through the Hugging Face API, reads selected text columns with optional PyArrow, filters for English integer-final-answer rows without recognized image/diagram cues, and converts them to ShortAnswerCreate. Existing credits provide seen source IDs. It collects the selected batch before writing, so a network failure during collection saves none of the new problems. Downloads retry selected errors with backoff. The image filter is heuristic and source answer keys are not independently verified. Evidence: tests/test_import_problems.py; tests/test_import_online.py, which mocks network access. Live source availability is not a claim of these tests.

Teacher tools and student practice
have separate permissions
The API checks stored roles. Login selects a profile using name and grade.

How achieved: main.py places most routers inside an /api router with Depends(get_current_user). dependencies.py reads the token from a nonempty access_token cookie first, or a bearer header, verifies signature/expiry/audience, and loads the User. get_teacher and get_student require the stored role. The management-question router has a router-wide teacher dependency. Assignment management and roster endpoints also require teacher access. Student check and own assignment endpoints require student access. Student response schemas omit keys during routine browsing, while AnswerFeedback reveals them after a check. Login returns an expiring signed JWT and sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie. The name/grade rule assigns teacher access to brian/12 and does not verify identity ownership. Students may check any bank question. Sources: backend/main.py; backend/dependencies.py; backend/security.py; backend/schemas.py; backend/services/auth.py. Evidence: tests/test_auth.py; tests/test_questions.py; tests/test_assignments.py; tests/test_bank.py.

Three tables preserve
the current assignment state
SQLite persists data. Services validate references and commit complete changes.

How achieved: SQLAlchemy models map User to profiles, Question to problems, and AssignedProblem to assigned_problems. The assignment pair is a composite primary key and references real profile/question rows. SQLite connection setup enables foreign-key enforcement. Deleting a question cascades to its assignment links. Assignment services also verify that target profiles have the student role, which a foreign key alone cannot establish. Request-scoped sessions close after use; services explicitly commit successful writes. User IDs use SQLite AUTOINCREMENT to avoid selecting a replacement profile with an old token. Login casefolds names/grades in SQL, while the database unique constraint uses stored spelling, so it is not a concurrency guarantee for normalized profiles. Startup create_all creates missing tables and does not migrate old schemas. Sources: backend/models.py; backend/database.py; backend/services/assignments.py. Evidence: tests/test_foundations.py; tests/test_assignments.py.

Mathematical practice
remains readable on the page

KaTeX renders formulas in prompts
and explanations. The original text
remains if the library is unavailable.

Responsive layouts fit narrow screens.
Loading and feedback states explain
what is happening after an action.
Text uses DOM textContent. Teacher solutions render math when expanded.

How achieved: frontend/styles.css defines layout breakpoints at 800px and 600px, wrapping controls, stacking editor fields, and adapting problem cards/assignment actions. frontend/app.js inserts server-provided strings with textContent rather than treating them as raw HTML. renderMath uses KaTeX auto-render with dollar and LaTeX delimiters, throwOnError:false, and trust:false. Student cards render displayed math, while teacher answer details wait until expanded. Pagination limits visible cards and associated math work. UI code supplies loading states, button disabling during operations, error notices, and stale-request counters so old responses do not overwrite newer views. This slide describes implemented UI behavior, not a completed accessibility audit or device/browser compatibility certification. Sources: frontend/index.html; frontend/styles.css; frontend/app.js. Evidence: tests/frontend-pagination.test.cjs math-call and request-failure checks.

Clear layers make
request behavior traceable
Validate inputs and select output fields
Apply workflow rules and commit writes
One FastAPI process serves the static frontend and the JSON API.

How achieved: main.py serves / through FileResponse, mounts frontend assets at /static, registers public /api/auth operations, and registers protected routers under /api. The frontend request helper uses relative /api URLs with same-origin credentials, so no separate frontend server or build system is required. Routers delegate most work to services, schemas define request/response contracts, database.py owns engine/session plumbing, and pure grading remains independent of HTTP/SQLAlchemy. A small student roster SELECT intentionally lives directly in the users router. ARCHITECTURE.md documents the design and backend-guide.html contains a source-linked walkthrough. These are maintainability/inspectability properties, not claims about a measured maintenance-time reduction. Sources: backend/main.py; backend/routers/; backend/services/; backend/schemas.py; backend/database.py; frontend/app.js; ARCHITECTURE.md.

Automated tests verify
the important workflows
Coverage includes grading, permissions, persistence, assignments, paging, and imports.

Evidence from the repository review on November 8, 2026: .venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider completed with 165 passed and one dependency deprecation warning about FastAPI TestClient/HTTPX. node --test tests/frontend-pagination.test.cjs completed with 4 passed. node --check frontend/app.js succeeded. Backend fixtures create isolated in-memory engines and override dependencies/startup, so normal tests do not use the local application database. Frontend tests execute the real JavaScript in a Node VM with a small simulated DOM and stubbed paginated API. Import tests mock remote calls. Coverage includes invalid inputs, hidden keys, role restrictions, repeatable checks without writes, data persistence, validation-before-assignment-replacement, question-deletion cascade, pagination totals, cross-page selection, import deduplication, and no partial network-failure batch. Test counts are not code-coverage percentages, browser visual certification, concurrency-load results, or proof of learning outcomes. Sources: tests/conftest.py; tests/test_*.py; tests/frontend-pagination.test.cjs; pyproject.toml.

One API request
across the whole stack

The helper adds "/api" and calls
fetch("/api/me") with GET.
The browser sends its login cookie.

FastAPI matches the route.
A dependency loads the user.
UserPublic selects the JSON fields.
The parsed JSON returns to openRoom(user), which selects the role’s view.

Detailed execution: opening / makes the browser request HTML. The script tag requests /static/app.js. Its final start() calls request('/me'). In app.js request(path,...) passes `/api${path}` to fetch, so path='/me' produces /api/me. Method defaults to GET. The path is rooted at the current website origin. On the backend, main.py creates APIRouter(prefix='/api', dependencies=[Depends(get_current_user)]) and includes users.router. users.py registers @router.get('/me', response_model=UserPublic), which combines with the prefix. get_current_user validates the cookie/header token and loads the row. A valid user returns JSON; an absent/invalid token returns 401. The frontend parses response.json. On success start passes the user to openRoom; on failure it shows login. Submitting login later sends POST /api/auth/login through the same helper. Server prefix registration and frontend URL construction are separate declarations that must agree. Sources: frontend/index.html:13; frontend/app.js request/start/openRoom; backend/main.py:35–40; backend/routers/users.py; backend/dependencies.py.

A complete local platform
for assigned practice

Teacher-managed assignments
A reusable, searchable problem bank
Immediate student feedback

The implementation combines a plain browser interface
with a validated Python API and persistent storage.

The finished scope is a functional local practice-and-assignment application. It provides individualized current assignments, a teacher-managed shared bank, supported question formats, filtering/paging, mathematical display, validated content imports, persistent relational storage, role checks, and automated behavior tests. Scope boundaries: name/grade selects a profile and does not establish verified account ownership; responses and completion history are not stored; short-answer grading compares normalized strings rather than mathematical equivalence; adaptive recommendations are absent; README.md describes deployment as a later setup rather than documenting a verified live production deployment. The deck intentionally makes no claims about adoption, improved grades, reduced teacher workload, scale benchmarks, or production security certification. Sources: README.md; ARCHITECTURE.md; backend/models.py; backend/services/grading.py; backend/services/auth.py. The completed implementation meets the defined local workflow goals.
